text:
Since coming back from injury, Logan Mailloux has looked like a different defenseman: 9 points in 8 games, 19:29 a night (up from 16:46 last season), and on the ice for 40% of the Blues' power-play chances after 7% a year ago. In Montreal, Hockey30 is already calling the trade that sent him to St. Louis Kent Hughes' worst.

Our numbers say the surge is earned, not just lucky. His own chances are up to 0.65 expected goals per 60 minutes from 0.19, and the Blues are getting about 59% of the 5-on-5 chance quality with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net more than 93% of defensemen last season, so the shooting instincts were always there. The caution is the sample. Eight games is tiny, and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in 2025-26 with his team's offense near the bottom of the league when he played. Ice time settles faster than scoring, which is why our numbers still project a modest 30 points. Keep an eye on whether he holds that power-play spot.
headline: Logan Mailloux has turned his return into a breakout
